lesson_title: VAT Calculations: the Fifteen Percent Hiding in Every Price
hook_text: A tracksuit costs R391 with VAT inside. Take 15% off to find the real price? Congratulations, you just failed the question.
clip_script: Every price in the shop hides a tax. The tracksuit says R391 — but that's the price WITH the government's fifteen percent already baked in. Now the exam asks: what did it cost before VAT? Almost everyone does the natural thing — take fifteen percent off. 15% of 391 is 58,65, subtract, get R332,35. Wrong. Here's why: the fifteen percent slice was cut from the SMALLER number, the before-tax price — not from 391. Slice the big number and you cut too deep. The real move: R391 is 115% of the original, so DIVIDE by 1,15. That's R340 exactly. The VAT hiding inside? R51. And prove it — 340 times 1,15 runs straight back to 391. If your answer can't run forwards, it's wrong. One more secret from your till slip: brown bread, maize meal, milk, eggs — zero percent VAT, on purpose. White bread? Taxed. Frozen chips? Taxed. So sort the slip before you calculate. VAT on: times 1,15. VAT out: divide by 1,15. Never subtract fifteen percent. Ever.
visual_style: A till slip unrolling down the screen, standard-rated lines lighting up with red stars while zero-rated basics glow green; a loaf of bread gaining and losing a 15% slice; the wrong answer R332,35 stamped out and R340,00 stamped in.
mood: Streetwise and protective, the voice of someone who checks the slip before leaving the till.
pacing: Fast into the trap, a dead stop on the wrong answer, deliberate and clear through the divide-by-1,15 fix and the zero-rated reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make the 15% work for your marks, not against them.
